chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them) that Ali (peace be upon him) said:

When a man marries a woman, her daughter becomes forbidden to him if he has had intercourse with the mother; and if he has not had intercourse with the mother, there is no harm in him marrying the daughter. But when he marries the daughter and has intercourse with her, or even if he has not had intercourse with her, the mother becomes forbidden to him. And he said: 'Your stepdaughters are forbidden to you, whether they are under your guardianship or not.'
ai.seo_question: Does a man's marriage to a woman make her daughter forbidden to him even if he hasn't consummated the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between marriage contract (nikah) and consummation (dakhala) in establishing prohibitions, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding step-relations. It confirms that while the mother becomes forbidden upon marrying the daughter regardless of consummation, the daughter remains permissible until the mother is consummated, reflecting the principle that 'bi-l-islakh' (by marriage) alone is insufficient for the daughter's prohibition without 'bi-l-waqi'' (by intercourse). The mention of 'in al-hajar' (under guardianship) underscores the juristic consensus that the bond of marriage itself, not just cohabitation, creates the mahram relationship.
